name: Gold real yield allocation
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Linking Gold to Real Yields
caseLead: Gold often benefits from falling real yields because lower inflation-adjusted interest rates reduce the opportunity cost of holding an asset that pays no income. Central bank reserve purchases and demand for assets outside the financial system also support prices, especially when sanctions or geopolitical tensions increase concerns about reserve security.
caseRest: Gold's relationship with real yields is not stable enough to explain every price move. Central bank purchases and demand for safe assets can support prices even when real yields are high, as in 2024 and 2025. Conversely, higher yields combined with a stronger US dollar have contributed to large declines, including in 2013 and 2022, so the allocation remains exposed to substantial short-term losses.
figNote: Each card shows the price of gold in US dollars per ounce at the close of the peak or trough of the episode. Gold is priced in dollars and pays no income, so its price reflects what investors expect to earn from holding other assets instead.

events.title: US downgrade and euro crisis lift gold
events.text: The US credit rating downgrade and the euro area debt crisis lifted gold to about 1,900 dollars in September 2011 as real yields fell. The strategy gained because lower real yields reduce the cost of holding gold, which pays no interest.

events.title: Gold falls 9% in one day
events.text: Gold fell 9% on 15 April 2013 to about 1,360 dollars, its largest one-day fall since 1980, as investors sold gold funds and inflation expectations fell. The strategy lost because lower inflation expectations and a firmer US dollar weakened the case for holding gold.

events.title: Fed rate rise sends gold to five-year low
events.text: Gold fell to about 1,050 dollars in December 2015, a five-year low, as the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time since 2006. The strategy lost because higher US real yields and a stronger dollar reduced demand for gold.

events.title: Zero rates push gold to a record high
events.text: Gold reached a record of about 2,070 dollars in August 2020 as the Federal Reserve held rates at zero and the 10-year real yield fell to minus 1.1%. The strategy gained because negative real yields reduce the cost of holding gold.

events.title: Real yields and the dollar push gold lower
events.text: Gold fell to about 1,620 dollars in September 2022 as the 10-year US real yield rose from minus 1% at the start of the year to above 1.5%. The strategy lost because higher real yields and a 20-year high in the dollar both weighed on gold.

events.title: US tariffs lift gold above 3,500 dollars
events.text: Gold reached about 3,500 dollars in April 2025 as US tariffs weakened the dollar and central banks kept buying. Results were mixed because real yields near 2% limited the allocation while the other signals supported it.

instrument: Gold futures and gold-backed ETFs; rebalanced monthly
rules: Gold weight set from the 10-year US real yield, the US dollar trend and central bank gold purchases; raised when real yields fall and reduced when they rise; put options bought on the position
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads, commissions and fund fees deducted at each monthly rebalance
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from real yield signals to loss limits

legs.purpose: Earns the return linked to real yields
Holds gold without roll costs when the signal is strong
Limits losses in a sharp fall in the gold price
Provides collateral and earns the cash rate

entry: 10-year real yield below its 12-month average and a stable or weaker dollar
size: Set to a 13% annualised volatility target
exit: Position halved when the real yield exceeds its 12-month average by 30 basis points
stop: Position closed if gold falls 12% from its monthly high
marketWatch: The 10-year US real yield, the US dollar index and central bank gold purchases are key indicators. Rehyn also tracks sanctions on reserve assets and geopolitical tension because they can raise official demand for gold without any change in real yields. Federal Reserve meetings and inflation data matter most because they move real yields within hours.

favourable.heading: Falling real yields
favourable.text: Falling real yields favour the strategy because they reduce the return on inflation-protected bonds, so gold becomes relatively more attractive. In 2019, the 10-year real yield fell by about 1 percentage point and gold rose by about 18%.

favourable.heading: Central bank gold buying
favourable.text: Official purchases favour the strategy because central banks buy regardless of price, which provides steady demand that is not tied to real yields. Central banks bought more than 1,000 tonnes a year in each year from 2022 to 2024, helping lift gold to records while real yields were high.

favourable.heading: A weaker US dollar
favourable.text: A weaker dollar favours the strategy because gold is priced in dollars, so it becomes cheaper for buyers in other currencies. In the first half of 2025, the dollar index fell by about 11% and gold rose by about 25%.

adverse.heading: Rapid rises in real yields
adverse.text: Rapid increases in real yields hurt the strategy because they raise the cost of holding gold and prompt sales by funds. Between April and June 2013, the 10-year real yield rose from about minus 0.7% to about 0.5% and gold fell by about 20%.

adverse.heading: A break in the link with yields
adverse.text: A break in the link with real yields hurts the strategy because the model can reduce gold exposure just as other buyers lift prices. In 2024, real yields stayed above 1.8% while gold rose by about 27%, so an allocation based on real yields alone missed much of the gain.

adverse.heading: Forced selling in a market crisis
adverse.text: A rush for cash hurts the strategy because investors sell gold to meet margin calls elsewhere, even though it is a defensive asset. In March 2020, gold fell by more than 10% in ten days as the dollar rose.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in real yields, the US dollar and the gold price, which are then applied to the strategy's current positions, including the protective options.
